cohort: 345 pregnant women with placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) at a single medical center, enrolled between August 2019 and February 2022.
finding: Emergency cesarean sections in women with placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) resulted in worse perinatal outcomes for both mothers (higher bleeding and blood transfusion) and neonates (lower birth weight, shorter length, smaller gestational age, higher incidence of severe asphyxia) compared to planned cesarean sections.
mod_finding: The study found that emergency cesarean sections, when compared to planned cesarean sections, significantly worsened maternal outcomes (increased bleeding and transfusion) and neonatal outcomes (reduced birth weight, length, gestational age, and higher asphyxia) in pregnancies complicated by Placenta Accreta Spectrum.
